heading: Advances are not Loans
memo_rationale: Retain the substantive risk allocation, but state a mutual contractual rule rather than requiring Merchant to certify a legal conclusion. The heading “Advances” also differs from a purchase.
memo_replacement: The parties agree to the nonrecourse allocation in the granting clause and Section 2.1. Buyer assumes the risk of insufficient Purchased Receipts and indefinite collection duration. Merchant does not warrant that a court or regulator will adopt the parties’ intended legal characterization. Nothing in this Section waives a statutory protection or defense.
current_body: Merchant fully understands that the Purchase Price is not a loan, but a non-recourse transaction pursuant to which Buyer’s funds are at full risk of non-payment in the event Receipts are not sufficient to satisfy the Purchased Amount, and that it is not possible to determine the time period within which the Specified Percentage of Receipts will last to satisfy the Purchased Amount.
my_note: Fine. Do not ask a merchant to certify a legal conclusion; state the allocation as a mutual contractual rule. Also correct the 'Advances' heading, which contradicts the purchase characterisation in the heading itself.

heading: Financial Condition and Financial Information
memo_rationale: An ongoing no-material-adverse-change promise and automatic material breach for slow records can shift ordinary business risk back to Merchant. Restrict factual accuracy to when furnished and require practical, purpose-limited reporting.
memo_replacement: To Merchant’s knowledge after reasonable inquiry, financial records furnished by Merchant are authentic and fairly present the matters they purport to show as of their stated dates, subject to identified qualifications. Merchant shall disclose material corrections discovered before funding. After funding, Merchant shall provide existing records reasonably necessary to verify Purchased Receipts within ten Workdays of a specific request, with reasonable extensions for unavailable records or circumstances outside its control. A later adverse change in financial condition, sales, or operations is not a breach of representation or an Event of Default. Records duties and remedies remain subject to Sections 3, 4.3, and 6.
current_body: Merchant’s bank and financial statements, copies of which have been furnished to Buyer, and any future statements that may be furnished, fairly represent the financial condition of Merchant at the dates indicated, and since those dates there has been no material adverse change, financial or otherwise, in Merchant’s condition, operation, or ownership. Merchant has a continuing affirmative obligation to advise Buyer of any material adverse change in its financial condition, operation, or ownership. Buyer may request statements at any time during the performance of this Agreement, and Merchant shall provide them within five (5) business days after the request. Merchant’s failure to provide them is a material breach of this Agreement.
my_note: An ongoing no-material-adverse-change covenant in a product that claims to bear the risk of non-generation is close to self-contradictory. Restrict accuracy to when furnished.

heading: Governmental Approvals
memo_rationale: The absolute all-laws/no-tax-lien representation is broader than necessary and could attach personal liability to an unknown tax or technical licensing problem. Keep material compliance information relevant to the purchased pool, allow disclosure/contests, and avoid warranting future solvency.
memo_replacement: To Merchant’s knowledge after reasonable inquiry, Merchant holds the material approvals needed for its disclosed business and is not subject to an undisclosed legal restriction that prevents this sale. Merchant has disclosed material known tax liens affecting Purchased Receipts and material unpaid taxes, excluding amounts lawfully deferred or contested in good faith. Merchant shall use reasonable efforts to maintain approvals necessary for its lawful operations. A later lien, tax dispute, or loss of approval is not itself an Event of Default absent conduct independently satisfying Section 6.1.
current_body: Merchant is in compliance with, and shall comply with, all applicable federal, state, and local laws and regulations, and has all valid permits, authorizations, and licenses necessary to own, operate, and lease its properties and to conduct the business in which it is presently engaged. Merchant has filed all federal, state, and local tax returns required to be filed and has paid all taxes shown thereon to be due and payable, except for taxes being contested in good faith and for which adequate reserves have been provided. Merchant has no outstanding tax liens against any of its assets or Receipts.
my_note: An absolute all-laws, no-tax-lien representation can attach personal liability to an unknown technical licensing lapse. Materiality and a contest right.

heading: Authorization
memo_rationale: An ordinary authority representation is appropriate. Obtain entity authority and verify the actual signatory; the clause does not substitute for diligence or a separate personal guaranty signature.
current_body: Merchant, and the person(s) signing this Agreement on behalf of Merchant, have full power and authority to incur and perform the obligations under this Agreement, all of which have been duly authorized.
my_note: Retain. Note the memo's dependency: this does not substitute for verifying the actual signatory or for a separate guarantor signature — which is exactly what 084 says we cannot currently see.

heading: Insurance
memo_rationale: The exclusion of business-interruption insurance is favorable. Because the proposed collateral is only a percentage of card receivables, a property/casualty loss-payee requirement is usually a poor fit. Delete as a conservative simplification; insurance on equipment belongs in the equipment document.
memo_replacement: Buyer does not require insurance guaranteeing the Purchased Amount or Merchant’s future receipts. No insurance policy is assigned by this Agreement. Separate equipment insurance requirements, if any, are governed solely by the equipment agreement and do not secure this purchase or create a default hereunder.
current_body: To the extent Merchant maintains property or casualty insurance covering the Collateral, Merchant will name Buyer as loss payee as to the Collateral and will provide proof of that coverage on request. Merchant is not required to carry business-interruption insurance for Buyer’s benefit, and Buyer takes no interest in any policy that would pay Buyer because Merchant’s Receipts have fallen.
my_note: Agree with deletion. When the collateral is a percentage of card receivables, a property-casualty loss-payee requirement is a poor fit and creates a covenant we will not monitor. Equipment insurance belongs in the equipment document.

heading: The Account
memo_rationale: “Any other action” with any adverse effect is an unbounded covenant. The immediate material-breach label conflicts with notice/cure and ordinary operational changes. Consolidate with §2.4.
memo_replacement: Changes to an account or processor affecting Purchased Receipts are governed exclusively by Section 2.4. Merchant shall reasonably cooperate to maintain the agreed split and shall not intentionally divert Purchased Receipts. No account change or adverse operational effect alone creates an Event of Default.
current_body: Merchant will not change the Approved Bank Account or take any other action that could have any adverse effect upon Merchant’s obligations under this Agreement, without Buyer’s prior written consent. Any such change shall be a material breach of this Agreement.
my_note: 'Any other action' with any adverse effect is an unbounded covenant with an immediate material-breach label. Consolidate into §2.4.

heading: Estoppel Certificate
memo_rationale: One day is impractical, and an unqualified estoppel could suppress reconciliation or disputed balances. A reasonable confirmation should let Merchant state disagreements and should not replace Buyer’s ledger.
memo_replacement: On at least ten Workdays’ written notice, Merchant shall reasonably cooperate in confirming the identity of this Agreement and amounts shown in available records. Buyer shall first provide its proposed statement and supporting ledger. Merchant may identify modifications, disputes, qualifications, and pending reconciliation. Failure to sign a disputed or inaccurate statement is not an Event of Default, admission, waiver, or confirmation of the Purchased Amount remaining uncollected.
current_body: Merchant will at any time, upon at least one (1) day’s prior notice from Buyer, execute, acknowledge, and deliver to Buyer or to any other person specified by Buyer a statement certifying that this Agreement is unmodified and in full force and effect (or, if there have been modifications, stating the modifications) and stating the dates which the Purchased Amount or any portion thereof has been delivered.
my_note: One day is not a workable confirmation window and an unqualified estoppel could suppress a live reconciliation dispute. Allow the merchant to state disagreement.

heading: No Bankruptcy
memo_rationale: A representation that Merchant does not contemplate bankruptcy can chill lawful advice and become recourse for future distress. Limit to known filed proceedings before funding, with no covenant against seeking relief. [A1–A4, A19]
memo_replacement: Merchant has disclosed any bankruptcy petition filed by it, or to its actual knowledge filed against it, that is pending on the Purchase Date. Merchant makes no representation about whether it may later seek restructuring or bankruptcy advice or relief. Seeking advice, insolvency, and a later filing are not Events of Default and do not create guarantor liability. All rights remain subject to applicable bankruptcy law.
current_body: As of the date of this Agreement, Merchant does not contemplate and has not filed any petition for bankruptcy protection under Title 11 of the United States Code, and there has been no involuntary petition brought or pending against Merchant.
my_note: A representation that the merchant does not contemplate bankruptcy chills lawful advice and functions as bankruptcy recourse. Limit to known filed proceedings at funding. This pairs with 087 — fixing one without the other leaves the clawback route open.

heading: No Encumbrance of Receipts
memo_rationale: This duplicates the negative pledge and improperly treats the affiliate equipment payment as a lien-ranking exception. Use one rule for the exact sold share.
memo_replacement: Restrictions on a further sale or voluntary encumbrance of Purchased Receipts are governed exclusively by Section 4.11. No equipment or subscription payment obtains security or priority under this Agreement.
current_body: Merchant shall not further encumber the Receipts without the prior written consent of Buyer, other than the monthly Equipment payment billed at merchant level by the Approved Processor under an Equipment Lease Agreement between Merchant and {{equipmentAffiliate}}, which is a permitted claim ranking after the Specified Percentage.
my_note: Duplicates 028 and repeats the equipment lien-ranking error. One rule for the sold share.

heading: Business Purpose
memo_rationale: Business purpose and actual recipient location determine legal coverage; a label or inaccurate good-standing representation cannot avoid consumer law. The form should work for properly identified sole proprietors as well as entities. Verify actual use and management location. [A8–A14]
memo_replacement: Merchant enters this transaction primarily for a lawful business or commercial purpose, and the proposed use of proceeds is accurately stated in Section 1. If Merchant is an entity, its legal form and organization jurisdiction are stated there; if a sole proprietor, that status and legal owner are identified. Section 1 accurately states Merchant’s principal place of business and the location from which the business is principally directed or managed. Buyer shall verify the facts needed to determine applicable law. This statement does not convert a primarily personal, family, or household transaction into a business transaction or waive any applicable protection.
current_body: Merchant is a valid business in good standing under the laws of the jurisdictions in which it is organized and operates, and Merchant is entering into this Agreement for business purposes and not as a consumer for personal, family, or household purposes. Merchant’s principal place of business is the Business Address stated in Section 1.1.
my_note: Adopt, and make the form work for a properly identified sole proprietor — we will see them and the current form assumes an entity.

heading: Civil/Criminal/Regulatory Matters
memo_rationale: The pending-proceedings limb lacks a knowledge qualifier and the continuing lead-in makes future litigation a breach. Limit to material known proceedings affecting this sale and permit disclosures.
memo_replacement: Merchant has disclosed proceedings pending, or to its actual knowledge threatened, that materially affect its authority to enter this Agreement or its ability lawfully to sell the Purchased Receipts as of the Purchase Date. This is not a warranty against future litigation, an adverse outcome, or a decline in Merchant’s business, and any remedy is subject to Sections 6 and 9.
current_body: There are no civil or criminal proceedings pending before any court, government agency, arbitration panel, or administrative tribunal, or, to Merchant’s knowledge, threatened against Merchant, that may result in any material adverse change in the business, property, or financial condition of Merchant.
my_note: Add a knowledge qualifier; the continuing lead-in otherwise makes any future litigation a breach.

heading: Business Closure
memo_rationale: A six-month lookback covering every temporary closure can capture vacations and ordinary repairs. Protect against deliberately concealed permanent closure at funding without promising that the business will continue.
memo_replacement: Merchant has disclosed any firm decision, existing on the Purchase Date, to permanently discontinue the business from which the Purchased Receipts are expected to arise. A prior temporary closure, ordinary renovation, seasonal shutdown, or later good-faith decision to close is not a breach. Merchant does not promise to operate for a minimum period.
current_body: At no time during the six (6) months immediately preceding the date of this Agreement has Merchant decided to close or cease operating its business, in whole or in part, temporarily or permanently.
my_note: A six-month lookback covering every temporary closure captures vacations and repairs. Aim at concealed permanent closure at funding.

heading: No Diversion of Receipts
memo_rationale: The daily all-receipts deposit obligation reaches cash/checks and ignores weekends, chargebacks, and settlement delays. Preserve a genuine anti-diversion covenant confined to generated Purchased Receipts and ordinary settlement availability.
memo_replacement: Merchant shall maintain agreed instructions for Approved Processors to remit Purchased Receipts in the ordinary settlement cycle and shall account for Purchased Receipts actually received by Merchant under Section 7.16. Merchant shall not intentionally conceal or divert that purchased share to defeat Buyer’s ownership. Ordinary settlement delays, refunds, chargebacks, processor reserves, bank holidays, disclosed changes under Section 2.4, and good-faith commercial decisions are not diversion. Non-card receipts and Merchant’s retained percentage are not subject to a daily deposit or remittance obligation under this Agreement.
current_body: Merchant must deposit all Receipts into the Approved Bank Account on a daily basis and must instruct Merchant’s credit card processor (which must be approved by Buyer) to deposit all credit and debit card Receipts of Merchant into the Approved Bank Account on a daily basis, net only of the Specified Percentage remitted to Buyer under Section 2.3 and of the monthly Equipment payment billed at merchant level by the Approved Processor under an Equipment Lease Agreement between Merchant and {{equipmentAffiliate}}, which is a permitted claim ranking after the Specified Percentage. Merchant agrees not to: (i) change the Approved Bank Account without the express written consent of Buyer; (ii) add an additional Account; (iii) close the Approved Bank Account without the express written consent of Buyer; or (iv) take any other action with the intent to interfere with Buyer’s right to collect the purchased Receipts.
my_note: A daily all-receipts deposit duty reaching cash and cheques, ignoring weekends and settlement lag, is unperformable — and an unperformable covenant paired with a default clause is a trap. Confine to generated Purchased Receipts.

heading: Change of Name or Location or Sale or Closing of Business
memo_rationale: An absolute ban on voluntary temporary closure and consent to every move can force continued operation to ensure repayment. Protect identification, successor settlement instructions, and existing purchased assets without making normal closure a default.
memo_replacement: Merchant shall give reasonable advance notice of a planned legal-name, organization-jurisdiction, processor, or principal-location change materially affecting Purchased Receipts, and prompt notice when advance notice is impracticable. For a proposed sale of substantially all of the relevant business, Merchant shall reasonably cooperate to disclose the transaction and preserve Buyer’s lawful interest in Purchased Receipts already sold, including a successor split arrangement where lawfully agreed. No transfer of unrelated assets or ordinary-course sale requires Buyer’s consent. Merchant may make good-faith operating, renovation, relocation, temporary-closure, and permanent-closure decisions. Those decisions do not themselves create an Event of Default, a repurchase duty, or liability for receipts never generated. Intentional fraudulent transfer or diversion remains subject to Section 6.1.
current_body: Merchant will not conduct Merchant’s businesses under any name other than as disclosed to Buyer, or change any of its places of business, without prior written consent of Buyer. Merchant will not voluntarily sell, dispose, transfer, or otherwise convey all or substantially all of its business or assets without (i) the express prior written consent of Buyer, and (ii) the written agreement of any purchaser or transferee assuming all of Merchant’s obligations under this Agreement pursuant to documentation satisfactory to Buyer. Except as disclosed to Buyer in writing, Merchant has no current plans to close its business either temporarily or permanently. Merchant will not voluntarily close its business on a temporary basis for renovations, repairs, or any other voluntary purposes. This provision does not prohibit Merchant from closing its business temporarily if such closing is required to conduct renovations or repairs that are required by local ordinance or other legal order, or if otherwise forced to do so by circumstances outside of the control of Merchant. Prior to any such closure, Merchant will provide Buyer ten (10) calendar days’ notice to the extent practicable.
my_note: An absolute ban on voluntary temporary closure can be read as compelling a merchant to keep trading to fund repayment, which is the worst possible fact in a recharacterization case.
